articles.summary: After Walt Z, a Michigan pizza store worker, went viral for standing up to the harassment of an influencer in the name of a prank video, social media
articles.body: After Walt Z, a Michigan pizza store worker, went viral for standing up to the harassment of an influencer in the name of a prank video, social media users speculated that the video may cost Walt Z his job. But Red Baron Pizza announced that Walt is still working and now he has a fan club. The pizza store also floated making Walt the employee of the month. The GoFundMe fundraiser, meanwhile, raised more than $450K and is nearing $500K now.Why did the Michigan father go viral?An influencer made a prank video featuring Walt Z pretending to steal money from Walt. The video begins with the influencer asking Walt Z for the time while he is stocking Red Baron pizzas into a grocery store freezer. As Walt Z pulls out his phone to check, the influencer plays a chime that mimics an Apple Pay transaction, then declares that he just stole $10 from Walt Z.“You’re probably making money off of this. And I can’t even pay my goddamn mortgage. And I’ve got four kids at home," Walt Z said.“Life is hard enough as it is. I don’t need this crap.” Walt also said that he was already one hour late and still had a lot of work.The influencer asked him to hold and said it was all a joke.The video, initially shared on Instagram by an account operating under the handle @thea.ctiveworld, also known as Three Of A Kind, sparked widespread criticism. The account appeared to have been deactivated following the backlash.After the video went viral, strangers came together to start a fundraiser for Walt. Luke Oakenshield, who started the fundraiser, said he did not know Walt personally but wanted to help him and his family. After the fundraiser got huge donations, he said he connected with Walt. GoFundMe also confirmed that they are working with Oakenshield to make sure Walt Z gets the money.A spokesperson for Red Baron’s parent company, Schwan, told The New York Post that Walt Z is a direct store delivery employee, adding that the viral incident occurred sometime in August.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Turns out murder is legal in India’: Sister seeks answers after her 24-year-old brother dies in alleged hit-and-run in Delhi, questions non-functional CCTV cameras
articles.summary: A 24-year-old man returning home after a night shift never made it back.
articles.body: A 24-year-old man returning home after a night shift never made it back. Six days after his death in a suspected hit-and-run in Delhi, his family is still searching for the vehicle involved and the person responsible. Now, his sister has raised questions over the functioning of CCTV cameras installed on city roads, alleging that several cameras along the stretch where the incident took place were either not working or did not have hard disks to store footage.In a video appeal shared on social media, Diya Singhal expressed her frustration over the family's struggle to obtain CCTV footage that could help identify the vehicle involved in the incident. Her appeal has also brought attention to a larger concern: whether road surveillance cameras are adequately maintained and can serve their purpose when evidence is urgently needed."Turns out murder is legal in India," Diya said in the video, expressing her anguish over the family's experience as it tries to find answers.What happened to Prince Singhal?According to the account shared by Diya, her younger brother, Prince Singhal, was returning to his home in Pitampura, Delhi, after completing his night shift at an office in Gurugram on October 24, 2026. The suspected hit-and-run took place near Naraina Flyover, opposite the Border Roads Organisation (BRO), between approximately 4:15 am and 4:45 am. "On 24 October 2026, my younger brother, Prince Singhal, was returning home to Pitampura, Delhi, after completing his night shift at his office in Gurgaon. He never made it home," she wrote in her social media appeal.Six days after the incident, the family was still trying to establish what happened and identify the vehicle allegedly involved.Diya has specifically appealed to people who travelled along Naraina Flyover towards Mayapuri during the early hours of October 24. She has asked commuters to share any information, eyewitness accounts or dashcam recordings that could help the investigation.Sister questions functioning of CCTV camerasDiya has alleged that despite cameras being present along the road, the family has been unable to obtain the footage it needs.Questioning why surveillance cameras are installed on public roads if they cannot help in situations like this, she said, "Camera sadkon par sirf challan kaatne ke liye hi hain. Kyunki vahi camera jab aaj mujhe apne bhai ke hit and run ke murderer ko pakadne ke liye unki jarurat hai, toh unme hard disk nahi hai."She also described the difficulties the family allegedly encountered while approaching the police for CCTV footage."Police ke paas hum gye toh vo keh rahe hain ki koi camera kharab hai, Kisi camera mein harddisk nahi hai, kisi camera ka angle theek nahi hai, koi camera chal hi nahi raha hai, aur koi camera kisi aur vibhaag ke under hai," she said.Her allegations point to several possible obstacles in obtaining surveillance footage, including non-functional cameras, missing storage devices, unsuitable camera angles and jurisdictional issues.Family appeals for dashcam footageWith the availability of CCTV footage in question, Diya has urged people who travelled through the stretch around the time of the suspected incident to check whether their vehicles recorded anything.Her appeal specifically seeks information from commuters travelling through Naraina Flyover towards Mayapuri between 4:15 am and 4:45 am on October 24.She has asked people to come forward if they witnessed the incident, noticed anything unusual or have dashcam footage that could help identify the vehicle."There are CCTV cameras around the flyover, and footage from vehicles travelling through this stretch could be crucial to the investigation," she wrote.The family is hoping that someone who passed through the area that morning may have inadvertently recorded the incident or captured the vehicle involved.For Diya and her family, the search for footage is part of a larger struggle to find answers following Prince's death."I am Diya Singhal, Prince's sister. My mother and I have lost someone we can never replace. We are not asking for sympathy alone; we are asking for help in finding answers and seeking justice for my brother," she wrote.As the family continues its search for information, the circumstances of the suspected hit-and-run and the identity of the vehicle involved remain to be established. For them, even a few minutes of footage from a passing vehicle or a functioning surveillance camera could help answer the questions that have remained unanswered since Prince left work that morning.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: Airbnb spends millions on Los Angeles mayoral race as it wants easier rental rules; company aims to deliver on the Olympics growth 'promise' it told investors to expect
articles.summary: Airbnb is spending millions to influence Los Angeles politics.
articles.body: Airbnb is spending millions to influence Los Angeles politics. The company is backing Mayor Karen Bass and other candidates while seeking easier short-term rental rules before the 2028 Olympics. According to a Politico report, Airbnb and its non-profit arm have spent at least $12.6 million since last year across political campaigns, lobbying and charitable contributions requested by politicians.​The company has told investors that the Olympics could expand its Los Angeles business beyond the games. “We have more than a 50% increase in the amount of homes in Paris on Airbnb because we hosted for the Olympics,” chief executive Brian Chesky told analysts last year. He said Airbnb had similar expectations for Los Angeles, where Bass’s challenger, City Council member Nithya Raman, opposes loosening rental restrictions.​How much Airbnb has spent​Public filings cited by the report show Airbnb has directed at least $6.9 million towards campaigns this election cycle. Most went to political action committees supporting Bass, while $2.1 million backed a committee supporting city attorney candidate John McKinney.​Those campaign contributions form part of the broader $12.6 million total. Airbnb also spent $3.7 million on its Save Our Services lobbying campaign, which argued that expanded vacation rentals could generate tourist taxes to help address the city’s budget shortfall.​Separately, its charitable arm provided $1 million worth of emergency housing at Bass’s request for families affected by a warehouse fire in Boyle Heights.​Airbnb’s North American policy strategy director, Nathan Rotman, said the company supports candidates who see home-sharing as a way for residents to meet housing costs.​“We’ve always supported candidates who champion solutions to the affordability crisis,” he told Politico.​What rental changes Airbnb wants​In 2018, Los Angeles adopted rules allowing short-term rentals only in primary residences. Airbnb has sought permission to expand to a wider range of properties.​Bass proposed allowing vacation rentals in second homes and investment properties through 2028. Her administration also proposed letting Airbnb pay anticipated Olympics-related taxes in advance to help cover the city’s current deficit.​The City Council rejected the rental expansion when it approved the budget in May.​Opponents include tenant advocates concerned about losing long-term housing, neighbourhood groups frustrated by party houses, and hotel industry representatives. Council member Katy Yaroslavsky criticised Airbnb’s lobbying tactics, including campaign flyers that did not identify the company.​Why the mayoral contest matters​Raman has made Airbnb’s spending and Bass’s proposed rental changes campaign issues. She has characterised the relationship as pay-to-play politics and promised a new city department to oversee home-sharing and penalise violations. Bass’s campaign rejects those allegations and says her proposed changes would help accommodate Olympics visitors.​Airbnb’s interest extends beyond that temporary demand. Chesky has told analysts that some first-time Olympics hosts continue renting their properties after the event, making major sporting occasions a way to increase listings. Rotman said the company would continue working with city officials regardless of the election result.​“At the end of the day, we will work closely with any mayor or City Council that gets elected,” he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Academic says he has been barred from UK over event with Palestine Action founder
articles.summary: Andreas Malm was due to appear on a panel alongside a co-founder of the proscribed group next week.
articles.body:
A Swedish climate academic says he has been barred from entering the UK because he was due to speak on a panel with a co-founder of Palestine Action.

Andreas Malm told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that he had received a letter from the Home Office notifying him that his presence was "not conducive to the public good", with no further details given.

He said he could not "see any other explanation" for being denied entry than his scheduled appearance with Huda Ammori, a founder of the group, which is a proscribed terrorist organisation in the UK.

The Home Office said it did not comment on individual cases.

Malm is a senior lecturer in human ecology at Sweden's Lund University, whose work includes the 2021 book How to Blow up a Pipeline and 2025's The Destruction of Palestine is the Destruction of the Earth.

He said he had asked the Home Office to explain its decision, but could not see a reason beyond the upcoming talk in London with Ammori organised by the left-wing magazine Tribune - calling the move a "severe restriction on the free exchange of ideas".

Malm said he was not a member of Palestine Action, had never publicly endorsed it, nor had he given it any financial support.

"The only link to Palestine Action is her as a person," he said, criticising the UK government for ascribing "guilt by association".

The academic acknowledged that he had previously described the Hamas-led 7 October 2023 attacks on Israel - in which about 1,200 people were killed and another 251 taken hostage - as "fundamentally an act of liberation".

Malm said it was possible that these remarks, during a December 2023 talk in which he also condemned the "deplorable" killing of civilians in the cross-border attack, had been the reason for the Home Office's decision.

But he argued that these views had been in the public realm for a long time, including when he was last allowed into the UK to deliver a talk in May.

"I don't expect the British state to agree with me on Palestine or climate or anything. What I expect the British state to do is to continue to let me enter the country and to discuss with colleagues, with people who disagree with me - as I have done for years."

Sally Rooney books withdrawn in UK over Palestine Action support

The UK Supreme Court is due to review Palestine Action's controversial ban under terrorism legislation . The Home Office has said that it will robustly defend against the appeal.

More than 3,700 people are believed to have been arrested in the UK over alleged support of the group. About 2,500 have been charged, though none have gone to trial as the legal challenge to the proscription continues.

The government has broad discretion to bar foreign nationals from entering the UK if their presence is deemed to pose a risk to society.

In April, 11 people described by then-Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer as "far-right agitators" were banned from entering the UK ahead of a rally led by Tommy Robinson.

Kanye West was also denied entry that same month after backlash to his planned set at London's Wireless Festival, following a string of antisemitic, racist and pro-Nazi comments. He had previously apologised for the remarks and said his bipolar disorder had caused him to lose "touch with reality".

Left-wing political commentators Hasan Piker and Cenk Uygur claimed in June that their visas had been revoked ahead of planned appearances in London and Oxford, allegedly "for criticising Israel" .

articles.title: Form 7 row: Supreme Court directs EC to probe bulk applications during Uttar Pradesh SIR
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday directed the Election Commission (EC) to examine allegations of irregularities in the bulk submission of Form 7
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday directed the Election Commission (EC) to examine allegations of irregularities in the bulk submission of Form 7 applications during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Uttar Pradesh and take necessary corrective measures.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the petitioners to submit a note to the EC detailing the "unresolved irregularities" they had flagged."The irregularities which have been brought to the notice of the court shall be submitted to senior counsel appearing for the Election Commission of India by way of a note. On receipt thereof, let the Election Commission examine the factual aspects, thereafter take necessary corrective steps and file a compliance report," the bench said, according to PTI.The Supreme Court was hearing petitions filed by Congress MP Tanuj Punia and others challenging the SIR exercise in Uttar Pradesh. More than 13 crore electors were included in the final electoral roll ahead of the assembly elections scheduled in the state early next year.The opposition has alleged that over 2.04 crore names were removed from the electoral rolls during the revision.During the hearing, counsel for the petitioners alleged that 32 Form 7 applications had been submitted in one constituency to target members of a particular community.Senior advocate DS Naidu, appearing for the EC, acknowledged that bulk Form 7 applications had been filed but said no action had been taken on them."We found that bulk Form 7 applications had been submitted. Our officers checked and cross-checked them. They were false, and we have not acted upon them," Naidu told the court.Following the submissions, the CJI-led bench directed the EC to examine the matter.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Assam will never return to those dark days’: Himanta recalls 2008 serial blasts, pays tributes to victims
articles.summary: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma pays tribute to 88 victims of 2008 serial blasts, vows peace; nine blasts killed 88, 500+ injured; NDFB convicts.
articles.body: Guwahati: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Friday paid tribute to the 88 victims of the October 30 serial blasts in 2008, vowing that the state would never return to the era of violence and bloodshed.Describing the day “one of the darkest chapters in Assam’s history,” the chief minister wrote on X, “I can never forget that fateful day which shook the collective conscience of our nation and remains one of the darkest chapters in Assam’s history.”He added, “We shall never return back to those days and ensure that Assam remains a peaceful and prosperous state in the years to come.”On October 30, 2008, nine coordinated explosions ripped through Guwahati, Kokrajhar, Barpeta Road and Bongaigaon, killing 88 people and injuring more than 500, many maimed for life. The blasts were carried out by the Ranjan Daimary faction of the National Democratic Front of Bodoland (NDFB).The attacks comprised three blasts each in Guwahati and Kokrajhar, two in Barpeta Road and one in Bongaigaon, making it one of the deadliest terror strikes in Assam.A special CBI court convicted 15 people in January 2019, sentencing 10, including NDFB chief Ranjan Daimary, to life imprisonment.
